paragraphs: The 420d has been a mainstay of the 4 Series diesel range since the model launched in 2013, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F32/F33/F36 cars (roughly 2013 to 2015) use the N47 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel that's shared across BMW's range of that era. From 2015, the F-generation 420d switched to the B47, a newer four-cylinder diesel that's significantly more reliable. The current G22/G23/G26 generation (2020 onwards) uses a B47 with mild-hybrid technology, which is a further evolution of that unit. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 420d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the 420d from 2013 to 2015. Known for timing chain failure — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N47 rebuild.
The later 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted from 2015. A significantly more reliable engine than the N47 it replaced, with no equivalent timing chain pattern.
The current 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel, fitted with mild-hybrid technology from 2020. B-series generation, generally reliable — no confirmed major issue pattern.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW 420d can use the B47 or N47 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47, B47 or B47 MHEV) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 420d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
